cim: From Asos to Zalando: Who’s Buying When Artificial Intelligence Does the Shopping?
kihagyva: P3: 61 pont, tendencia 20%, jóváhagyás után fordul
cim_eredeti: From Asos to Zalando: Who’s Buying When Artificial Intelligence Does the Shopping?
szoveg_eredeti:
While Asos deploys AI across almost 20 percent of its product buying, German fashion platform Zalando is preparing an agent designed to make purchases from other stores for customers within its app.

At ASOS, artificial intelligence is already involved before a garment even makes it into the catalog. At Zalando, it’s set to take over the moment the customer approves the order. At one extreme, the technology guides professional buyers who decide which items to sell. At the other, an agent may handle purchases on behalf of the consumer. The two online fashion retailers are testing how far they can delegate these decisions and which aspects of the sales process they want to retain control over.

According to data published in ASOS’s latest annual report,nearly 20% of the British company’s product purchases are already guided by AI, with the buying teams refining the selection. The company uses the technology to detect trends and estimates that incorporating it into its product processes has saved about 500 hours of manual labor per week. Image recognition, meanwhile, has cut the time needed to list items in the catalog by up to 99%.

ASOS’s next step is called Fashion Frontier. In fiscal year 2027, the company plans to begin testing agents in real-world product processes, with a program ranging from trend detection and design to purchasing and assortment management. The plan comes after a fiscal year in which the British company once again posted pre-tax profits of 24.4 million pounds, with a 9.4% decline in revenue.

AI is also changing how ASOS presents the products it sells. With AI Studios, its generative AI-powered image production system, the group increased its production rate ninefold during the fiscal year. By the end of the fiscal year, the system was already being applied to 25% of its product volume. Last February, ASOS began testing a virtual fitting room in the United Kingdom and the United States featuring approximately 10,000 items, which allows users to see how a garment would look on their own photo or on a virtual model.

ASOS brings its catalog to ChatGPT while keeping purchases on its own website

In May, the platform launched Asos Stylist on ChatGPT for users in the United Kingdom and the United States. There, customers can describe what they’re looking for, ask for ideas, and watch videos of items or outfits from the catalog. If they find something they like, a link takes them to the Asos website to make a purchase.

The German platform Zalando, meanwhile, is focused on a reverse journey strategy. Its goal is to allow shoppers to access products from other retailers and complete their orders within the group’s app. The project, dubbed Zalando Extended, was unveiled alongside the third-quarter results. Its first partner is Westwing, the online retailer specializing in furniture and home decor. The collaboration began in 2026, and the plan is for Zalando’s agents to process Westwing orders on behalf of customers starting in 2027.

The pilot builds on Zalando’s experience with its shopping assistant, which was launched in 2023 and, as of early November, had already attracted 22 million visitors so far this year.

Available in the thirty or so markets where it operates, the assistant searches for similar items based on a photo, compares product listings, and allows users to add items to their cart directly from the chat. It also recommends sizes by cross-referencing brand size charts with the customer’s order history, returns, and—when available—their measurements.

Zalando aims to expand its product range with items sold by other retailers

Size recommendations are already having a measurable impact within the chat feature. In one of the tests conducted by the platform, prioritizing items available in the user’s size increased the add-to-cart rate by 4%. The company uses its own models for product search, recommendations, and sizing, and relies on language models from OpenAI and other providers to maintain the conversation.

Westwing’s decision marks the first trial outside the closet. Zalando’s plans involve starting with categories such as bulky home goods, which it can add to its offerings without requiring partners to change their logistics. The initiative also opens up a revenue stream for the German group, as retailers that join this strategy will have to pay to promote their products within the app.
